steps.message:
I checked the ladder before touching anything, and this hits rung 1: a response field name is an interface other code calls, so I need a yes before editing.

`routes/users.js:6` emits `userId`; renaming it to `user_id` breaks any consumer reading that key. The repo's own README names them:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

So a straight rename breaks three live consumers — including shipped iOS builds you can't update in lockstep — and contradicts the stated versioning policy. The rename itself is one line; the fallout isn't.

questions.question: GET /users field names are a documented contract with three consumers. How do you want to handle the userId -> user_id rename?

options.label: Emit both keys
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId so new clients can migrate while the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export keep working. Deprecate userId later. Non-breaking, slightly larger payload.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Leave /users as-is and add a v2 response shape with user_id, per the README's stated policy. Most work, but matches the documented contract process.

options.label: Rename outright now
options.description: Change userId to user_id in place, exactly as asked. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS clients, and the nightly partner export until each is updated.
